'''Willie D. Warren''' (born October 22, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]].

==High school career==
After a successful high school career at [[North Crowley High School]], Warren was selected to be a [[McDonald's All-American]]. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Warren was listed as the No. 4 point guard and the No. 10 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Willie-Warren-42534 Willie Warren Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Warren then went to the [[University of Oklahoma]] where he played on the same team as his eventual Clippers teammate, [[Blake Griffin]]. Despite being a projected lottery pick after a successful Freshman year, Warren stayed at OU, hoping to be the primary option with Griffin leaving for the draft. Throughout an injury-plagued Sophomore year he averaged over 16 points, 4 assists, 3 rebounds and just over 1 steal a game while shooting above 30% from 3-point range . At the end of his sophomore season, Warren decided to forgo his last two years of eligibility, signing with an agent and declaring for the [[2010 NBA draft]].

==Professional career==
Warren was drafted late in the 2nd round as the 54th overall by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on the day of the [[2010 NBA draft]]. Then, on July 13, 2010, he was signed by the Clippers.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_secondround_signs_100713.html CLIPPERS SIGN 2010 SECOND ROUND PICK WILLIE WARREN]</ref>

Late in the 2010–11 season, Warren was assigned to the NBA D-League. There, he played 6 games in 2011 for the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA D-League]] where he averaged 21.0 points, 7.0 assists, 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game while shooting above 50 percent from the field and 46 percent from 3-point range. The Jam went 5–1 with Warren in the lineup from February 4 – 16. After the D-League stint, Warren was called back into the Clippers' line-up, but he was later reassigned for a second stint on March 2, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/warren_110203.html |title=NBA Development League: Clippers Assign Willie Warren To Bakersfield Jam |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213054252/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/warren_110203.html |archive-date=2012-02-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 19, 2011, Warren was waived by the Clippers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-waive-warren-ahearn-koch-major-111219.html CLIPPERS: CLIPPERS WAIVE WARREN, AHEARN, KOCH AND MAJOR]</ref>

In August 2012, Warren signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli Super League]] for the 2012–13 season.<ref>[https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/basketball.aspx?NewsID=282890 Maccabi Rishon Lezion signs American PG Willie Warren]</ref>

In the summer of 2013, he signed with [[Szolnoki Olaj KK]] of Hungary.<ref>[http://www.szolnokiolaj.hu/Hir.aspx?h=1583 A Szolnoki Olaj Kosárlabda Klub a mai napon egyéves szerződést kötött Willie Warren-nel.]</ref> On February 28, 2014, he was waived by Szolnoki.<ref>{{cite news|title=Szolnoki Olaj waive Willie Warren|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/hungary/112444/szolnoki-olaj-waive-willie-warren.html|access-date=28 February 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref> On March 4, 2014, he signed with [[Virtus Bologna]] of Italy for the rest of the [[2013–14 Lega Basket Serie A]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Granarolo Bologna announces Willie Warren until 2015|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/112832/granarolo-bologna-announces-willie-warren-until-2015.html|access-date=25 March 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=4 March 2014}}</ref>

On September 18, 2014, Warren signed with [[Chongqing Fly Dragons]] of [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/135073/willie-warren-signs-with-chongqing-fly-dragon.html Willie Warren signs with Chongqing Fly Dragon]</ref> On April 16, 2015, he signed with [[Hekmeh BC|Club Sagesse]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/158564/willie-warren-agreed-to-terms-with-sagesse.html Willie Warren agreed to terms with Sagesse]</ref> However, he never joined the Lebanese team due to an injury.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/159090/sagesse-signs-brandon-heath.html |title=Sagesse signs Brandon Heath |access-date=2015-04-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620173828/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/159090/sagesse-signs-brandon-heath.html |archive-date=2017-06-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On August 6, 2015, Warren signed with [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/171813/willie-warren-inks-with-zhejiang-chouzhou.html Willie Warren inks with Zhejiang Chouzhou]</ref> He later re-signed with Zhejiang for one more season.

On August 13, 2017, Warren signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mirza Begic and Willie Warren ink in Iran with Petrochimi|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/244218/mirza-begic-and-willie-warren-ink-in-iran-with-petrochimi.html|access-date=August 13, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=August 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170917124456/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/244218/mirza-begic-and-willie-warren-ink-in-iran-with-petrochimi.html|archive-date=September 17, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

On December 9, 2017, Warren signed with the [[Shanxi Brave Dragons]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2017-12-09/doc-ifypnsip2185688.shtml|title=山西官宣:因成绩不理想更换外援 沃伦替詹宁斯|work=Sina.com|language=zh|date=December 9, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2017}}</ref>

On February 22, 2018, Warren was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Legends Complete Trade with Clippers|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-complete-trade-with-clippers/n-5297631|access-date=April 1, 2018|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 22, 2018}}</ref> but was waived on March 23 after playing three games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Texas Legends waive Willie Warren|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/g-league/267117/texas-legends-waive-willie-warren.html|access-date=April 1, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=March 7, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On June 30, 2019, he has signed with [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/willie-warren-signs-with-al-riyadi/|title=Willie Warren signs with Al Riyadi|date=June 30, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 1, 2019|last1=Lupo|first1=Nicola|archive-date=August 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807200018/https://sportando.basketball/en/willie-warren-signs-with-al-riyadi/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
